scope: Model/editor Quality v3 remediation review of EN-A1-L-0027; not an independent human or real-learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: In the explicit phone-photo context, Who is she? / She is Maya. and Who is he? / He is Alex. are natural identification exchanges; Coffee? / Yes, please. is an established cafe interaction rather than a forced target prompt.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Persian consistently maps he/she identification to conversational اون while instructional feedback explicitly distinguishes the male/female English pronouns without adding unsupported meaning.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: Dialogue-dependent tasks are ordered after exposure, duplicate exact-sentence assessment is practice-only, and hidden-answer retrieval remains the strongest evidence.

distractorQuality.evidence: Distractors isolate pronoun choice, name choice and first-person versus third-person meaning, so mistakes reveal a specific misunderstanding rather than random vocabulary confusion.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: Generic story metadata was replaced where needed by scene copy grounded in the canonical setting and turns.

difficultyFit.evidence: The lesson follows We are from Lesson 26 with one closely related A1.1 be-pattern and familiar character names, keeping cognitive load controlled.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: Repeated exact target sentences may remain for practice, but only the strongest occurrence is scored; this reduces false mastery from repeated identical answers.

transferQuality.evidence: Guided practice identifies Maya and Alex, response choice contrasts she/he for Maya, and final hidden retrieval requires She is Sara. with a familiar but previously unused name filler.

overallCoherence.evidence: The cafe recurrence, photo-identification scenario, support questions, pronoun contrast, reconstruction and changed-name retrieval all serve one communicative outcome.

learnerExperience.evidence: Runtime ordering and answer tolerance were improved, but no real learner test is claimed.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
The Lesson does not establish the full pronoun or be paradigm and does not assess question inversion.
Who is she? and Who is he? are support formulas whose comprehension is scaffolded by the photo context rather than separately mastered.
Final ElevenLabs prosody and delayed retention remain unmeasured.
No independent human or real learner test has been performed after learner-context repair.
Quality v3 remediation was model/editor reviewed; real learner evidence is still required before public-release readiness.
resolvedFindings: Selected CEFR-J he/she is, the highest-ranked new grammar candidate in spec 0027, instead of adding a new lexical target.
Returned to Ava and Ben only after five intervening Lessons, satisfying the course-wide character rotation rule and continuing the latest cafe episode, Lesson 21.
Reused due coffee naturally in the cafe rather than forcing a due item into the identification target itself.
Kept Maya, Alex and Sara as familiar proper-name referents rather than lexical teaching rows; only Ava and Ben are speaking story participants.
Final retrieval changes the female name from Maya to Sara, preventing the target from remaining a memorized single phrase.
